results.name: Anonymous recordings are denied and a fresh owner receives an actual empty catalog
The dedicated recording path is bound using the actual publisher proof
A changed cookie account is rejected by the expected-owner header
Invalid catalog status, limit and cursor are rejected
A growing recording is listed but cannot be replayed or downloaded
Fresh recording catalog exposes only real completed files with measured duration and byte totals
Pre-existing files are not imported and another account sees no owning-channel recordings
Authenticated recording download returns the exact finalized raw file with no-store and attachment headers
Private media implements real HEAD, ranged HEAD, bounded and suffix byte ranges
Unsatisfiable, multiple and malformed ranges return 416 without full-file fallback
Every media request checks cookie ownership and the explicit expected owner
Recording details are private and no-store
An observed ownership-boundary recording remains explicitly unplayable
Finalized metadata survives a source-continuing API restart without adopting a valid pre-existing recording
Files spanning unverified recording boundaries stay restricted after source-continuing restart
Catalog visibility mutations require the real CSRF token
Another signed-in account cannot change a foreign recording catalog entry
Hiding a recording changes only catalog visibility and blocks playback without deleting raw bytes
Hidden recordings leave the normal catalog and appear in the actual hidden filter
Stale visibility revisions are rejected instead of overwriting the latest state
Restoring a catalog item re-enables its verified recording without changing the source file
An identical visibility request at the current revision is an actual no-op
A missing recording is reported from actual file disappearance and cannot leak cached bytes
A changed corrupt recording is re-probed and never served using stale ready metadata
A real directory junction escaping the configured recording root cannot serve even a byte-identical file
Search uses actual persisted recording catalog rows
Actual opaque cursor pages separate recorded files without duplicating rows
Actual private recording video, catalog mutations, failure recovery and responsive UI pass
Development StrictMode renders the same real recording metadata without mutation
The tested private JAR stays immutable throughout recording and restart verification
